metin: I'm asking one last time, {ad}. Back east with our kin, there's work for all of us.
okunus: I'm asking one last time. Back east with our kin, there's work for all of us.

metin: I don't know anywhere but these plains, Pa.
okunus: I don't know anywhere but these plains, Pa.

metin: I don't know anywhere but these plains, Pa.
okunus: I don't know anywhere but these plains, Pa.

metin: I know. Neither did I.
okunus: I know. Neither did I.

metin: Stop in and see Sully in town. He'll be asking after you.
okunus: Stop in and see Sully in town. He'll be asking after you.

metin: Thirty-one years since I first rode this road.
okunus: Thirty-one years since I first rode this road.

metin: Martha sat up on the wagon and I walked alongside. We couldn't afford a horse.
okunus: Martha sat up on the wagon and I walked alongside. We couldn't afford a horse.

metin: And now?
okunus: And now?

metin: And now?
okunus: And now?

metin: Now there's a horse.
okunus: Now there's a horse.

metin: ...No Martha.
okunus: ...No Martha.

metin: Anyway. The chickens are waiting on me, and me on them.
okunus: Anyway. The chickens are waiting on me, and me on them.

metin: Shh. You hear that?
okunus: Shh. You hear that?

metin: The wind?
okunus: The wind?

metin: The wind?
okunus: The wind?

metin: Wind doesn't carry off chickens.
okunus: Wind doesn't carry off chickens.

metin: Coyotes. Third night running. To the coop, quick!
okunus: Coyotes. Third night running. To the coop, quick!

metin: There's something I need to tell you. You deserve to hear it.
okunus: There's something I need to tell you. You deserve to hear it.

metin: Last month I was riding to the bank. Had the deed on me; needed to show it for a loan.
okunus: Last month I was riding to the bank. Had the deed on me; needed to show it for a loan.

metin: Three riders came out on the road. The one in front had a red beard. He was laughing.
okunus: Three riders came out on the road. The one in front had a red beard. He was laughing.

metin: What did they take?
okunus: What did they take?

metin: What did they take?
okunus: What did they take?

metin: My wallet. My watch. And the deed.
okunus: My wallet. My watch. And the deed.

metin: Whoever holds the deed holds the land, so they say. This house, those chickens, Martha's grave... all of it hangs on a scrap of paper.
okunus: Whoever holds the deed holds the land, so they say. This house, those chickens, Martha's grave... all of it hangs on a scrap of paper.

metin: Didn't you go to the sheriff?
okunus: Didn't you go to the sheriff?

metin: Didn't you go to the sheriff?
okunus: Didn't you go to the sheriff?

metin: I did. "I don't have the men, Sully," he says. Thirty years I paid my taxes, and he doesn't have the men.
okunus: I did. "I don't have the men, Sully," he says. Thirty years I paid my taxes, and he doesn't have the men.

metin: Anyway. Get up early tomorrow. The bank wants its interest, and the barn wants a roof.
okunus: Anyway. Get up early tomorrow. The bank wants its interest, and the barn wants a roof.

metin: Let me do the talking. The sheriff likes me.
okunus: Let me do the talking. The sheriff likes me.

metin: Well... he used to.
okunus: Well... he used to.

metin: Buy a drink at the bar. Then keep quiet.
okunus: Buy a drink at the bar. Then keep quiet.

metin: Keep quiet?
okunus: Keep quiet?

metin: Keep quiet?
okunus: Keep quiet?

metin: People can't stand silence. They'll say anything to fill it.
okunus: People can't stand silence. They'll say anything to fill it.

metin: At your age I slept on the ground like this too. My back hurt less.
okunus: At your age I slept on the ground like this too. My back hurt less.

metin: Why are you helping me, Sully? From the very first day.
okunus: Why are you helping me, Sully? From the very first day.

metin: Why are you helping me, Sully? From the very first day.
okunus: Why are you helping me, Sully? From the very first day.

metin: Couldn't say.
okunus: Couldn't say.

metin: Maybe I'm paying back the help nobody gave me. Maybe I was just looking for someone to talk to.
okunus: Maybe I'm paying back the help nobody gave me. Maybe I was just looking for someone to talk to.

metin: Eat something, then sleep. I'll keep watch; I can't sleep anyway.
okunus: Eat something, then sleep. I'll keep watch; I can't sleep anyway.

metin: Four of them. One on watch, and he's dozing.
okunus: Four of them. One on watch, and he's dozing.

metin: See the red one? By the fire, standing.
okunus: See the red one? By the fire, standing.

metin: I want him alive, {ad}. His corpse would give me back the deed, but it can't answer for anything.
okunus: I want him alive. His corpse would give me back the deed, but it can't answer for anything.

metin: And the others?
okunus: And the others?

metin: And the others?
okunus: And the others?

metin: The others are your call. I'll be with the horses; if I hear shots, I'll come.
okunus: The others are your call. I'll be with the horses; if I hear shots, I'll come.

metin: Thirty-one years... and a scrap of paper.
okunus: Thirty-one years... and a scrap of paper.

metin: Martha would've laughed. "Dunham, don't get so attached to paper," she'd say.
okunus: Martha would've laughed. "Dunham, don't get so attached to paper," she'd say.

metin: But you did.
okunus: But you did.

metin: But you did.
okunus: But you did.

metin: I did. But not to the paper.
okunus: I did. But not to the paper.

metin: This ranch's door is always open to you, {ad}. Come whenever you like. I'll even buy coffee this time.
okunus: This ranch's door is always open to you. Come whenever you like. I'll even buy coffee this time.

metin: Maybe someday I'll have land of my own again.
okunus: Maybe someday I'll have land of my own again.

metin: Maybe someday I'll have land of my own again.
okunus: Maybe someday I'll have land of my own again.

metin: You will. Just don't go carrying the deed around in your pocket like me.
okunus: You will. Just don't go carrying the deed around in your pocket like me.

metin: Thirty years. Every morning the same fire, the same coffee.
okunus: Thirty years. Every morning the same fire, the same coffee.

metin: Just once I'd like to wake up somewhere else.
okunus: Just once I'd like to wake up somewhere else.

metin: First time I rode up this ridge I was your age. A borrowed gun in my hand, nothing in my pocket.
okunus: First time I rode up this ridge I was your age. A borrowed gun in my hand, nothing in my pocket.

metin: Any regrets?
okunus: Any regrets?

metin: Any regrets?
okunus: Any regrets?

metin: Regret's a luxury, kid. I'm tired, that's all.
okunus: Regret's a luxury, kid. I'm tired, that's all.

metin: This is my last winter. Come spring, I'm done. Vance doesn't know, and he'd better not.
okunus: This is my last winter. Come spring, I'm done. Vance doesn't know, and he'd better not.

metin: Well, well. The old wolf sent the pup to town, and the pup came back unrecognized.
okunus: Well, well. The old wolf sent the pup to town, and the pup came back unrecognized.

metin: Tomorrow morning a mail coach comes through. The mining company's payroll is aboard.
okunus: Tomorrow morning a mail coach comes through. The mining company's payroll is aboard.

metin: Any guards?
okunus: Any guards?

metin: Any guards?
okunus: Any guards?

metin: A driver and a coward. Nobody dies, right, Hollis? He's gone soft with age.
okunus: A driver and a coward. Nobody dies, right, Hollis? He's gone soft with age.

metin: First turn what's left from the old job into cash. The fence doesn't ask questions. And change your look; your description is on everyone's lips in town.
okunus: First turn what's left from the old job into cash. The fence doesn't ask questions. And change your look; your description is on everyone's lips in town.

metin: I counted it. Twice. Half's mine, half's the gang's.
okunus: I counted it. Twice. Half's mine, half's the gang's.

metin: You are the gang, Silas.
okunus: You are the gang, Silas.

metin: Exactly, old man. Arithmetic isn't for everyone.
okunus: Exactly, old man. Arithmetic isn't for everyone.

metin: And I heard something: somebody's quitting come spring. Wonder who that could be?
okunus: And I heard something: somebody's quitting come spring. Wonder who that could be?

metin: I'm tired, Silas. That's all.
okunus: I'm tired, Silas. That's all.

metin: Tired men talk, Hollis. Men who talk hang.
okunus: Tired men talk, Hollis. Men who talk hang.

metin: Thirty years I sat by a fire waiting for the next job.
okunus: Thirty years I sat by a fire waiting for the next job.

metin: Now there's nothing to wait for. Strange. Light.
okunus: Now there's nothing to wait for. Strange. Light.

metin: Where will you go?
okunus: Where will you go?

metin: Where will you go?
okunus: Where will you go?

metin: West. I've never seen the ocean. Maybe I'll catch fish; maybe the fish will catch me.
okunus: West. I've never seen the ocean. Maybe I'll catch fish; maybe the fish will catch me.

metin: Find yourself a place, {ad}. A door, a fence, a pot of coffee. The things I never found.
okunus: Find yourself a place. A door, a fence, a pot of coffee. The things I never found.

metin: Take this revolver. I won't need it again; I hope you won't either.
okunus: Take this revolver. I won't need it again; I hope you won't either.

metin: Up! These rails won't lay themselves!
okunus: Up! These rails won't lay themselves!

metin: Sun's not even up yet, Boone.
okunus: Sun's not even up yet, Boone.

metin: Up before the sun, done before it sets. A new hand joins the crew today; set a good example.
okunus: Up before the sun, done before it sets. A new hand joins the crew today; set a good example.

metin: The slope slid in the night. The track is buried under rock.
okunus: The slope slid in the night. The track is buried under rock.

metin: If the line isn't open before the noon train, the company will throw half the crew out.
okunus: If the line isn't open before the noon train, the company will throw half the crew out.

metin: I have a pickaxe.
okunus: I have a pickaxe.

metin: I have a pickaxe.
okunus: I have a pickaxe.

metin: That'll do for the small ones. For the big one we need something else.
okunus: That'll do for the small ones. For the big one we need something else.

metin: The chest came. I counted it. Twice.
okunus: The chest came. I counted it. Twice.

metin: How short is it this time?
okunus: How short is it this time?

metin: A third. They wrote "losses." Travel costs, damp, rats...
okunus: A third. They wrote "losses." Travel costs, damp, rats...

metin: Rats eat money?
okunus: Rats eat money?

metin: Rats eat money?
okunus: Rats eat money?

metin: The company's do. Here, this is your share. Don't keep it at camp; money in a tent is like water in a bag: one morning it's gone.
okunus: The company's do. Here, this is your share. Don't keep it at camp; money in a tent is like water in a bag: one morning it's gone.

metin: I got word and came. When a man steals the crew's pay, the foreman doesn't stand aside.
okunus: I got word and came. When a man steals the crew's pay, the foreman doesn't stand aside.

metin: Move up behind the rocks. Take cover when you shoot; a man standing in the open doesn't live long.
okunus: Move up behind the rocks. Take cover when you shoot; a man standing in the open doesn't live long.

metin: I want Hale alive. Let him talk in court, in front of the company.
okunus: I want Hale alive. Let him talk in court, in front of the company.

metin: Twenty years I laid track. I always wanted to be on a train running over those rails one day; never happened.
okunus: Twenty years I laid track. I always wanted to be on a train running over those rails one day; never happened.

metin: Now I've bought my ticket. My daughter's out west, in a town on the coast. I have a grandchild; I don't even know the name.
okunus: Now I've bought my ticket. My daughter's out west, in a town on the coast. I have a grandchild; I don't even know the name.

metin: The crew is yours. Pay them in full, don't let Mick make the coffee, and always treat dynamite as the last resort.
okunus: The crew is yours. Pay them in full, don't let Mick make the coffee, and always treat dynamite as the last resort.

metin: The wagon?
okunus: The wagon?

metin: The wagon?
okunus: The wagon?

metin: I wrote "lost" to the company. It's yours now; haul your own freight, build your own crew.
okunus: I wrote "lost" to the company. It's yours now; haul your own freight, build your own crew.

metin: The rails run west, {ad}. One day you'll ride them too. Wave to this camp from the window.
okunus: The rails run west. One day you'll ride them too. Wave to this camp from the window.

metin: Four months, Anton. This is your last letter.
okunus: Four months, Anton. This is your last letter.

metin: Four months, Anton. This is your last letter.
okunus: Four months, Anton. This is your last letter.

metin: "When you reach Saint Clement, find Greta Halvorsen. She'll help you."
okunus: "When you reach Saint Clement, find Greta Halvorsen. She'll help you."

metin: "When you reach Saint Clement, find Greta Halvorsen. She'll help you."
okunus: "When you reach Saint Clement, find Greta Halvorsen. She'll help you."

metin: "Dear {ad}. I wrote that I'm at the mine in Silver Ridge, that the work is hard but the pay is good. I lied."
okunus: "My dear. I wrote that I'm at the mine in Silver Ridge, that the work is hard but the pay is good. I lied."

metin: "The company store sells everything on credit. Pickaxe, lantern, bread. Then it takes it out of your wages. It never stops taking."
okunus: "The company store sells everything on credit. Pickaxe, lantern, bread. Then it takes it out of your wages. It never stops taking."

metin: "A man named Pike keeps the ledger. Whatever I pay, my debt grows. I couldn't save for your passage, forgive me."
okunus: "A man named Pike keeps the ledger. Whatever I pay, my debt grows. I couldn't save for your passage, forgive me."

metin: "Don't come. Or come, but don't tell Pike my name."
okunus: "Don't come. Or come, but don't tell Pike my name."

metin: ...That fool. Why didn't he write to me?
okunus: ...That fool. Why didn't he write to me?

metin: Pride.
okunus: Pride.

metin: Pride.
okunus: Pride.

metin: Pride never got anyone out of debt. Silver Ridge is far; you can't walk there. You need a horse.
okunus: Pride never got anyone out of debt. Silver Ridge is far; you can't walk there. You need a horse.

metin: Look at that. Dust, rock and a lot of tired faces.
okunus: Look at that. Dust, rock and a lot of tired faces.

metin: Anton lived here for two years.
okunus: Anton lived here for two years.

metin: Anton lived here for two years.
okunus: Anton lived here for two years.

metin: Lived? People don't live here, {ad}. They pay off debts.
okunus: Lived? People don't live here. They pay off debts.

metin: The first year was good. I was saving money, I was going to buy your ship ticket.
okunus: The first year was good. I was saving money, I was going to buy your ship ticket.

metin: Then there was a cave-in. My leg broke; I couldn't work for two months. Pike said, "On credit." Smiling.
okunus: Then there was a cave-in. My leg broke; I couldn't work for two months. Pike said, "On credit." Smiling.

metin: And that smile never ended.
okunus: And that smile never ended.

metin: Pike ran. He took the company's payroll chest and holed up in the old gallery; he's waiting for his men.
okunus: Pike ran. He took the company's payroll chest and holed up in the old gallery; he's waiting for his men.

metin: He has the notes. Everyone's notes in town. As long as those papers exist, nobody is free.
okunus: He has the notes. Everyone's notes in town. As long as those papers exist, nobody is free.

metin: Then we take the papers.
okunus: Then we take the papers.

metin: Then we take the papers.
okunus: Then we take the papers.

metin: I was going to meet you at the pier when you stepped off the ship. Flowers in my hand, fare money in my pocket. That's how I imagined it.
okunus: I was going to meet you at the pier when you stepped off the ship. Flowers in my hand, fare money in my pocket. That's how I imagined it.

metin: And I imagined finding you in front of your own store.
okunus: And I imagined finding you in front of your own store.

metin: And I imagined finding you in front of your own store.
okunus: And I imagined finding you in front of your own store.

metin: Well. One of us got it right.
okunus: Well. One of us got it right.

metin: You two are cut from the same cloth. I'm going back to Saint Clement; a boarding house without lodgers is like a morning without coffee.
okunus: You two are cut from the same cloth. I'm going back to Saint Clement; a boarding house without lodgers is like a morning without coffee.

metin: I haven't forgotten your rent, Anton. But take your time. New beginnings aren't cheap.
okunus: I haven't forgotten your rent, Anton. But take your time. New beginnings aren't cheap.

metin: Mother always said: wherever you go, you take your roots with you. I think our roots have arrived, {ad}.
okunus: Mother always said: wherever you go, you take your roots with you. I think our roots have arrived.

metin: Six weeks now, Pa. The cabin's too quiet without you.
okunus: Six weeks now, Pa. The cabin's too quiet without you.

metin: Six weeks now, Pa. The cabin's too quiet without you.
okunus: Six weeks now, Pa. The cabin's too quiet without you.

metin: Elias Crowe has come down to town. If anyone can find you, he can.
okunus: Elias Crowe has come down to town. If anyone can find you, he can.

metin: Elias Crowe has come down to town. If anyone can find you, he can.
okunus: Elias Crowe has come down to town. If anyone can find you, he can.

metin: Frost fell last night. Winter's coming early this year.
okunus: Frost fell last night. Winter's coming early this year.

metin: Your father is up north, somewhere under the snow. Dead or alive, we'll find him.
okunus: Your father is up north, somewhere under the snow. Dead or alive, we'll find him.

metin: Alive.
okunus: Alive.

metin: Alive.
okunus: Alive.

metin: ...Alive. Have it your way.
okunus: ...Alive. Have it your way.

metin: Your father and I came to these woods the same winter. We were both seventeen, and both fools.
okunus: Your father and I came to these woods the same winter. We were both seventeen, and both fools.

metin: Our first winter a wolf pack surrounded our camp. Abel grabbed a log from the fire and yelled. The wolves ran.
okunus: Our first winter a wolf pack surrounded our camp. Abel grabbed a log from the fire and yelled. The wolves ran.

metin: My father? Yelled?
okunus: My father? Yelled?

metin: My father? Yelled?
okunus: My father? Yelled?

metin: Once. Then he didn't raise his voice for twenty years.
okunus: Once. Then he didn't raise his voice for twenty years.

metin: ...Shh. Hear that?
okunus: ...Shh. Hear that?

metin: The Old King. Standing up he's two men tall. His left ear is torn, a trapper's keepsake.
okunus: The Old King. Standing up he's two men tall. His left ear is torn, a trapper's keepsake.

metin: You won't drop him with one shot. Shoot from range, fall back, shoot again. Run and he'll run you down.
okunus: You won't drop him with one shot. Shoot from range, fall back, shoot again. Run and he'll run you down.

metin: And my father?
okunus: And my father?

metin: And my father?
okunus: And my father?

metin: When a bear guards a place, it's guarding either its food or its enemy. Pray it's the second.
okunus: When a bear guards a place, it's guarding either its food or its enemy. Pray it's the second.

metin: Six weeks. Every night I waited, I thought the same thing: "The kid can't read tracks."
okunus: Six weeks. Every night I waited, I thought the same thing: "The kid can't read tracks."

metin: Elias taught me.
okunus: Elias taught me.

metin: Elias taught me.
okunus: Elias taught me.

metin: Elias? He hasn't said more than two sentences to me in twenty years.
okunus: Elias? He hasn't said more than two sentences to me in twenty years.

metin: Not to you. To the kid.
okunus: Not to you. To the kid.

metin: The trapline is yours now, {ad}. I'll sit in the cabin giving you advice; you won't listen, and I'll grumble.
okunus: The trapline is yours now. I'll sit in the cabin giving you advice; you won't listen, and I'll grumble.

metin: Deal, Dad.
okunus: Deal, Dad.

okunus: Deal, Dad.
